node.date_label: Ward 1978 · Avery 1979 · Abella and Troper 1982 · Perin 1983 · Anderson 1991 · Walker on race and the law 1997 · Backhouse 1999 · selected publication milestones, not boundaries; coverage through 2000

date_span.basis: Selected publication milestones only. 1978 is the first selected milestone, not a field origin (the Multicultural History Society of Ontario dates from 1976); 1999 is the last selected in-period milestone. Post-2000 work sits in extension_coverage. Earlier Black Canadian works (Trudel 1960, Winks 1971) moved to cdn_black_history.

node.description: Studies immigration, ethnic communities, racism and the state in Canada: immigrant workers and their reception, ethnic identity, and the legal and spatial making of racial categories. The field expanded from the late 1970s. Ward's White Canada Forever (1978) traced west-coast prejudice against Asian residents and the discriminatory policies it produced; Avery's 'Dangerous Foreigners' (1979) examined European immigrant workers and labour radicalism; Abella and Troper studied Canada and the Jews of Europe, 1933–48 (1982). Perin's 'Clio as an Ethnic' (1983) asked whether ethnic groups had been 'discovered' just when the state faced challenges such as Quebec nationalism. Studies of Toronto neighbourhoods (Harney, who co-founded the Multicultural History Society of Ontario in 1976), Italian migrants in Montreal (Ramirez), Chinese Montrealers (Helly), Quebec's immigration policy (Pâquet 1997), British Columbia politicians (Roy), Italian immigrants in postwar Toronto (Iacovetta) and Ukrainian-Canadian women (Swyripa) followed. Anderson (1987, 1991) treated 'Chinese' and 'Chinatown' as racial categories made through government practice and place, which a reviewer saw as moving beyond earlier studies of white prejudice; Walker's Supreme Court case studies (1997) and Backhouse's Colour-Coded (1999) traced racism through law. Black Canadian history, including Black migration and immigration control, is a separate entry. Post-2000 work turned to Cold War reception and citizenship (Iacovetta 2006; Bohaker and Iacovetta 2009).
node.scope_note: A research field joining immigration and ethnic history with histories of racism. Black Canadian history is a separate proposed entry, cdn_black_history (user decision 2026-10-12, Q46); a short cross-reference strand keeps two works on Black migration and immigration control here. Indigenous–settler relations are in native_newcomer and settler_colonialism. Roster inclusion is not adoption of one framework: Ward's 'attitudes and public policy' and Anderson's 'racial category' approaches differ. A reviewer saw Anderson moving beyond earlier studies of white attitudes and prejudice (Stanley 1993); no checked text has Anderson distancing herself from White Canada Forever by name, so she is not listed as Ward's critic.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Ward, White Canada Forever (1978); Avery, "Dangerous Foreigners" (1979); Abella and Troper, None Is Too Many (1982); Palmer, Patterns of Prejudice (1982); Perin, "Clio as an Ethnic" (1983); Ramirez, Les premiers Italiens de Montréal (1984) and On the Move (1991); Harney, ed., Gathering Place (1985) and "So Great a Heritage as Ours" (1988); Anderson, "The Idea of Chinatown" (1987) and Vancouver's Chinatown (1991); Helly, Les Chinois à Montréal (1987); Taschereau, "L'histoire de l'immigration au Québec" (1988); Anctil, Le rendez-vous manqué (1988); Roy, A White Man's Province (1989); Iacovetta, Such Hardworking People (1992) and "Manly Militants" (1995); Knowles, Strangers at Our Gates (1992); Swyripa, Wedded to the Cause (1993); Avery, Reluctant Host (1995); Pâquet, Toward a Quebec Ministry of Immigration (1997); Walker, "Race," Rights and the Law (1997); Backhouse, Colour-Coded (1999). Black migration (cross-reference to cdn_black_history): Calliste, "Race, Gender and Canadian Immigration Policy" (1993–94); Shepard, Deemed Unsuitable (1997). Extension: Epp, Iacovetta and Swyripa, eds., Sisters or Strangers? (2004); Pâquet, Tracer les marges de la Cité (2005); Iacovetta, Gatekeepers (2006); Bohaker and Iacovetta (2009).

representative_people.name: W. Peter Ward
representative_people.context: Traces west-coast prejudice against Chinese, Japanese and East Indian residents and the discriminatory policies it produced.

representative_people.name: Donald Avery
representative_people.context: Studies European immigrant workers, labour radicalism and Canada's response to immigrant workers.

representative_people.name: Irving Abella
representative_people.context: With Harold Troper, studies Canada and the Jews of Europe, 1933–48.
representative_people.works: None Is Too Many (1982, with Troper)

representative_people.name: Harold Troper
representative_people.context: Co-author of None Is Too Many.
representative_people.works: None Is Too Many (1982, with Abella)

representative_people.name: Roberto Perin
representative_people.context: Questions the timing and politics of the "discovery" of ethnicity in Canadian historiography (opening argument read only).

representative_people.name: Bruno Ramirez
representative_people.context: Francophone and English-language studies of Italian and French-Canadian migrants in Montreal and the North Atlantic economy.
representative_people.works: Les premiers Italiens de Montréal (1984); On the Move (1991; French edition Par monts et par vaux, 1991)

representative_people.name: Robert F. Harney
representative_people.context: Co-founded the Multicultural History Society of Ontario in 1976 (with Milton Israel and others) and led it as president and academic director until his death in 1989; edited a collection on the peoples and neighbourhoods of Toronto.
representative_people.works: Gathering Place (1985, ed.); "So Great a Heritage as Ours" (Daedalus 1988)

representative_people.name: Kay J. Anderson
representative_people.context: A geographer who treats "Chinese" and "Chinatown" as racial categories constructed through government practice and place in Vancouver. A reviewer saw her racialization approach moving beyond earlier studies of white attitudes and prejudice, while noting that, like them, it says little about Chinese Canadians' own challenges to that discourse (Stanley 1993).

representative_people.name: Martin Pâquet
representative_people.context: Studies how the Quebec state defined the foreigner and the immigrant, from a CHA booklet on the road to a Quebec ministry of immigration (1997) to a long-run study, 1627–1981 (2005, extension). Thinly cited outside francophone universities.
representative_people.works: Toward a Quebec Ministry of Immigration, 1945 to 1968 (1997); Tracer les marges de la Cité (2005)

representative_people.name: Patricia E. Roy
representative_people.context: Studies British Columbia politicians and Chinese and Japanese immigrants.

representative_people.name: Franca Iacovetta
representative_people.context: Studies Italian immigrants in postwar Toronto, surveys historians' writing about immigrants, and later Cold War reception and citizenship.
representative_people.works: Such Hardworking People (1992); "Manly Militants" (1995); Sisters or Strangers? (2004, co-ed.); Gatekeepers (2006); "Making Aboriginal People 'Immigrants Too'" (2009, with Bohaker)

representative_people.name: Valerie Knowles
representative_people.context: A popular survey of Canadian immigration policy, widely cited in its later editions.
representative_people.works: Strangers at Our Gates (1992; later editions)

representative_people.name: Frances Swyripa
representative_people.context: Studies Ukrainian-Canadian women and ethnic identity.
representative_people.works: Wedded to the Cause (1993); Sisters or Strangers? (2004, co-ed.)

representative_people.name: Constance Backhouse
representative_people.context: Traces racism through Canadian law, 1900–1950. Primary placement: moral_regulation.

strands.title: Black migration and immigration control (cross-reference)
strands.focus: Black Canadian history is a separate entry (cdn_black_history). Kept here are two works on Black migrants and Canadian immigration control: Calliste on Caribbean workers and domestics, 1900–32, and the state's 'desire to exclude blacks as permanent settlers' (abstract read), and Shepard on African American migration from Oklahoma to the prairies before 1914.
strands.works: Agnes Calliste, "Race, Gender and Canadian Immigration Policy: Blacks from the Caribbean, 1900–1932," Journal of Canadian Studies 28, no. 4 (1993–94): 131–148.; R. Bruce Shepard, Deemed Unsuitable (Toronto: Umbrella Press, 1997).

strands.title: Immigrant workers, radicalism and migration
strands.focus: Immigrant labour, radicalism, and migrants between Quebec, Italy and New England; links to cdn_working_class.
strands.works: Donald Avery, "Dangerous Foreigners": European Immigrant Workers and Labour Radicalism in Canada, 1896–1932 (Toronto: McClelland and Stewart, 1979).; Bruno Ramirez, Les premiers Italiens de Montréal: l'origine de la Petite Italie du Québec (Montréal: Boréal Express, 1984).; Bruno Ramirez, On the Move: French-Canadian and Italian Migrants in the North Atlantic Economy, 1860–1914 (Toronto, 1991).; Donald H. Avery, Reluctant Host: Canada's Response to Immigrant Workers, 1896–1994 (Toronto, 1995).

strands.title: Immigration to Quebec
strands.focus: A small francophone literature on immigration to Quebec: Italian migrants in Montreal and the North Atlantic economy (Ramirez 1984; 1991, in English and French), Chinese Montrealers (Helly 1987), Jewish Montreal between the wars (Anctil 1988), Taschereau's 1988 RHAF essay inviting the field to move beyond community 'ghettos' (title level), and Pâquet on the Quebec state's definition of the immigrant (1997; Tracer les marges de la Cité, 2005, as extension coverage). In the 2009–2026 PhD corpus each work is cited by only 3–8 dissertations; Pâquet 2005 is the only one cited mostly at francophone universities (5 of 8). Laval is undercounted.
strands.works: Bruno Ramirez, Les premiers Italiens de Montréal (Montréal: Boréal Express, 1984).; Denise Helly, Les Chinois à Montréal, 1877–1951 (Québec: IQRC, 1987).; Sylvie Taschereau, "L'histoire de l'immigration au Québec: une invitation à fuir les ghettos," RHAF 41, no. 4 (1988): 575ff.; Pierre Anctil, Le rendez-vous manqué (Québec: IQRC, 1988).; Bruno Ramirez, Par monts et par vaux: migrants canadiens-français et italiens dans l'économie nord-atlantique, 1860–1914 (Montréal: Boréal, 1991).; Martin Pâquet, Toward a Quebec Ministry of Immigration, 1945 to 1968 (Ottawa: Canadian Historical Association, 1997).; Martin Pâquet, Tracer les marges de la Cité: étranger, immigrant et État au Québec, 1627–1981 (Montréal: Boréal, 2005).

strands.title: Racism, nativism and immigration policy
strands.focus: Popular prejudice, politicians and exclusionary policy, from British Columbia and Alberta to refugee policy.
strands.works: W. Peter Ward, White Canada Forever: Popular Attitudes and Public Policy toward Orientals in British Columbia (Montreal: McGill-Queen's University Press, 1978; 3rd ed. 2002).; Irving Abella and Harold Troper, None Is Too Many: Canada and the Jews of Europe, 1933–1948 (Toronto: Lester & Orpen Dennys, 1982).; Howard Palmer, Patterns of Prejudice: A History of Nativism in Alberta (Toronto: McClelland and Stewart, 1982).; Patricia E. Roy, A White Man's Province: British Columbia Politicians and Chinese and Japanese Immigrants, 1858–1914 (Vancouver: University of British Columbia Press, 1989).; Valerie Knowles, Strangers at Our Gates: Canadian Immigration and Immigration Policy, 1540–1990 (Toronto: Dundurn, 1992).

strands.title: Ethnic history and its critics
strands.focus: The politics of "discovering" ethnicity (Perin), community and neighbourhood studies and the Multicultural History Society of Ontario (Harney), and Iacovetta's review of how historians wrote about immigrants (title-level).
strands.works: Roberto Perin, "Clio as an Ethnic: The Third Force in Canadian Historiography," Canadian Historical Review 64, no. 4 (1983): 441–467.; Robert F. Harney, ed., Gathering Place: Peoples and Neighbourhoods of Toronto, 1834–1945 (Toronto, 1985).; Robert F. Harney, "'So Great a Heritage as Ours': Immigration and the Survival of the Canadian Polity," Daedalus 117, no. 4 (1988): 51–97 (issue number unconfirmed).; Franca Iacovetta, "Manly Militants, Cohesive Communities, and Defiant Domestics: Writing about Immigrants in Canadian Historical Scholarship," Labour/Le Travail 36 (1995): 217ff.

strands.title: Race as a category of law, place and state
strands.focus: Racial categories made through government practice, place and law, rather than taken as given. Timothy Stanley's review (1993) saw Anderson's racialization approach moving beyond earlier studies of white attitudes and prejudice, though he added that it shared their neglect of Chinese Canadians as actors.
strands.works: Kay J. Anderson, "The Idea of Chinatown: The Power of Place and Institutional Practice in the Making of a Racial Category," Annals of the Association of American Geographers 77, no. 4 (1987): 580–598.; Denise Helly, Les Chinois à Montréal, 1877–1951 (Québec: Institut québécois de recherche sur la culture, 1987).; Kay J. Anderson, Vancouver's Chinatown: Racial Discourse in Canada, 1875–1980 (Montreal and Kingston: McGill-Queen's University Press, 1991).; James W. St. G. Walker, "Race," Rights and the Law in the Supreme Court of Canada: Historical Case Studies (1997; Wilfrid Laurier University Press edition).; Constance Backhouse, Colour-Coded: A Legal History of Racism in Canada, 1900–1950 (Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 1999).

strands.title: Immigrant and ethnic women
strands.focus: Gender within immigrant families and ethnic communities; links to cdn_women_gender.
strands.works: Franca Iacovetta, Such Hardworking People: Italian Immigrants in Postwar Toronto (Montreal and Kingston: McGill-Queen's University Press, 1992).; Frances Swyripa, Wedded to the Cause: Ukrainian-Canadian Women and Ethnic Identity, 1891–1991 (Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 1993).; Marlene Epp, Franca Iacovetta and Frances Swyripa, eds., Sisters or Strangers? Immigrant, Ethnic, and Racialized Women in Canadian History (Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 2004).

strands.title: Reception, citizenship and the Cold War
strands.focus: Post-2000 work on gatekeepers and citizenship programmes, including their extension to Indigenous peoples.
strands.works: Franca Iacovetta, Gatekeepers: Reshaping Immigrant Lives in Cold War Canada (Toronto: Between the Lines, 2006).; Heidi Bohaker and Franca Iacovetta, "Making Aboriginal People 'Immigrants Too': A Comparison of Citizenship Programs for Newcomers and Indigenous Peoples in Postwar Canada, 1940s–1960s," Canadian Historical Review 90, no. 3 (2009): 427–462.

proposed_relationships.relationship: Race as a historically made category
proposed_relationships.map_label: Racial formation and Canadian race history
proposed_relationships.evidence_note: Anderson (1987, abstract read) treats racial categories as cultural ascriptions whose construction cannot be taken for granted and shows government inscribing 'Chinese' and 'Chinatown' in practice and space; racial formation treats race as historically specific and produced through social and political relations. Parallel, not derivation: PhD context shows Omi or Winant cited by 1 of 172 PhDs engaging this group (and by 7 of 1303 overall).

proposed_relationships.relationship: Ethnicity, recognition and the politics of its discovery
proposed_relationships.evidence_note: Perin's opening asks whether it is coincidence that ethnic groups were 'discovered' when the US faced the civil rights movement and Canada an assertive Quebec nationalism. The identity umbrella groups historical recovery with struggles over exclusion and recognition and is itself open to criticism. Comparison; Perin's full argument was not read.

Avery's 'Dangerous Foreigners' (1979; reviewed by Bruno Ramirez in International Labor and Working-Class History) and Ramirez's On the Move (1991) study immigrant workers; Iacovetta's 'Manly Militants' (1995) reviews how historians wrote about immigrants (title-level). PhD context: 97 of 142 2009–2026 PhDs engaging cdn_immigration_ethnicity also engage cdn_working_class (68%; lift 3.37), counted after removing shared anchors (Palmer). Bibliographies record consultation, not influence; lifts are high for most Canadian pairs.

Iacovetta (1992), Swyripa (1993) and Epp, Iacovetta and Swyripa, eds., Sisters or Strangers? (2004) work at the meeting of the two fields. Title-level. PhD context: 94 of 133 2009–2026 PhDs engaging cdn_immigration_ethnicity also engage cdn_women_gender (71%; lift 2.98), counted after removing shared anchors (Iacovetta). Bibliographies record consultation, not influence; lifts are high for most Canadian pairs.

proposed_relationships.relationship: Citizenship programmes for newcomers and Indigenous peoples
proposed_relationships.evidence_note: Bohaker and Iacovetta (abstract read) show that from 1950 to 1966 the Indian Affairs branch sat in the Department of Citizenship and Immigration and modelled its activities on citizenship campaigns for immigrants. A post-2000 comparison across the two fields. PhD context: 74 of 172 2009–2026 PhDs engaging cdn_immigration_ethnicity also engage native_newcomer (43%; lift 2.3), counted after removing shared anchors. Bibliographies record consultation, not influence; lifts are high for most Canadian pairs.

open_questions: Black Canadian history: keep it as a strand here (proposed), or create a separate Canadian Black history entry? groups.json lists 'Black Canadian history' among possible missing groups. Walker's 1997 essay treats it as its own historiography.
Correction to the request: Walker's 'Allegories and Orientations in African-Canadian Historiography' is Dalhousie Review 77:2 (1997), not CHR 1999.
Harney's 'So Great a Heritage as Ours' (Daedalus 1988) and his role in the Multicultural History Society of Ontario could not be verified; Gathering Place (1985) stands in for him.

Ward and Anderson: the draft notes that their approaches differ (attitudes and policy vs racial category) but does not make Anderson a critic of Ward, because no checked text says so. Should someone read Anderson 1991's introduction?
Knowles is a popular historian whose 2007 edition is what PhDs cite; keep her as a contributor row?

Francophone uptake is low (9 of 172 engaged PhDs at Montréal, UQAM, Laval and Sherbrooke). Ramirez and Helly are included; are there other francophone works the user wants (e.g. on immigration to Quebec)?

Walker keeps a row here for Race, Rights and the Law, with primary placement proposed for cdn_black_history. Description rewritten (within 150–250 words); date label and period rationale now start at 1978.
Already resolved: Walker's 'Allegories and Orientations' is cited as Dalhousie Review 77:2 (1997), checked in full text.

Harney's Daedalus essay is now cited as 117, no. 4 (1988): 51–97 from a citing article (issue number flagged as unconfirmed). Harney's row says he co-founded the MHSO in 1976 with Milton Israel and others and led it until his death in 1989 (MHSO page; AHA obituary).
